newsitem.title: USA: Mirage Resorts Q1 falls below consensus. [CORRECTED 2:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mirage Resorts Q1 falls below consensus. [CORRECTED 2:30 GMT]

text.p: Mirage Resorts Inc on Tuesday reported earnings of $0.29 a share, after adjustments, which fell slightly below financial analysts' estimates.
Analysts had expected Mirage to earn $0.31 a share with a range of estimates from $0.26 to $0.33, according to investment research firm First Call.

Mirage noted first quarter 1997 earnings compared to a strong year ago quarter at flagship hotel/casino, The Mirage, in Las Vegas which had "exceptionally high" levels of baccarat play last year. Indeed, 1997's first quarter was the second best in company history behind first quarter 1996, it said.
"The recent quarter also experienced a strong level of baccarat play, but with a more normal win percentage," Mirage said in a statement.
Baccarat is a card game that generates a lot of play from high-stakes gamblers, which can lead to wide swings in earnings depending on how lucky the casino and/or players are.

Across the company, the table game win percentage fell to 20 percent from 21.5 percent one year ago. For the full year 1996, the company posted a table game win percentage of 19.3 percent and in 1995, the figure was 20.2 percent.
Mirage's first quarter earnings included a charge of $0.01 a share for debt refinancing, offset by a gain of $0.01 per share for a land sale.
In the first quarter of 1996, Mirage earned $0.33 a share after a $0.03 per share gain for the sale of the company's interest in a casino in Argentina.

First quarter revenues totaled $394 million, down from $408 million one year ago. Revenues at The Mirage were $217 million versus $227 million. Excluding baccarat in both periods, total revenues were about equal to 1996, Mirage said.
In Las Vegas at Treasure Island, revenues were $101 million versus $105 million and at the Golden Nugget, they were $52.8 million versus $59.7 million.
The company's equity in the Monte Carlo hotel/casino, opened in summer 1996, generated revenue of $7.4 million.
In Laughlin, Nev., Mirage's Golden Nugget generated revenue of $15.9 million versus $16.7 million last year.

Operating cash flow and operating income were down at each of its properties. Total operating cash flow was about $113 million in the first quarter 1997 versus $128 million last year and operating income was $92 million versus $105 million.
Standard guest room occupancy in 1997's first quarter was 99.4 percent company wide versus 99.3 percent last year. The average guest room rate was $93 compared to $92.
The company's shares outstanding fell 5.2 million to a total 190.5 million versus 195.7 million last year, reflecting shares repurchased by the company in the second half of 1996.
